newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Real S.African house prices down 4.2 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Real S.African house prices down 4.2 pct in 1996.

text.p: The average price of South African houses fell by 4.2 percent in 1996 in real terms after a 2.4 percent decline in 1995, said the Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) in a quarterly housing review.
The average price of a house was 169,000 rand in nominal terms, three percent higher than in 1995 when it increased by six percent, Absa said.

It said the average price rise on a medium-sized house in nominal terms was higher compared with the preceding quarter. But, in real terms, the average price in this category fell for the seventh consecutive quarter by not less than 5.5 percent.
Year-on-year inflation stood at 9.4 percent in December.
Building costs in 1996 rose by 6.7 percent versus 5.1 percent in 1995. Absa said the rise probably contributed to the gap in the prices of new and existing houses.
Nominal mortgage rates fluctuated between 18.25 and 20.25 percent last year. Absa saw a tight monetary policy continuing this year and expected a cut in interest rates in the third quarter.
